Veolia Environnement SA Names New Chief Operating Officer in Senior Leadership Shift

PARIS, June 17—Veolia Environnement SA, a leading player in France’s utilities sector, announced Monday the appointment of Claire Martin as its new Chief Operating Officer, effective July 1. The move is part of a broader strategy to strengthen the company’s management team amid ongoing efforts to enhance operational efficiency across its gas and water services.

Martin, 52, brings more than two decades of experience in the utilities industry, most recently serving as deputy CEO at Lyonnaise Services, where she led major infrastructure projects and digital transformation initiatives. She is expected to report directly to Veolia’s Chief Executive Officer, Antoine Frérot.

“Claire’s track record in managing large-scale operations and driving innovation will be a tremendous asset to Veolia as we continue to adapt to evolving customer needs and regulatory requirements,” Frérot said in a statement.

Industry analysts welcomed the appointment, noting Martin’s reputation for fostering sustainable practices and stakeholder engagement. “Claire Martin’s expertise positions Veolia well as the sector faces increasing demands for environmental responsibility and operational resilience,” said Jean-Luc Bernard, senior analyst at Paris-based consultancy Utility Insights.

The French Gas & Water Utilities industry has been undergoing significant transformation in recent years, with companies investing in modernizing infrastructure, expanding digital services, and responding to regulatory pressures to reduce environmental impact. In 2023, Veolia reported revenues of €42.8 billion, with its water division accounting for just over half of total sales.

The French Association of Utility Workers also reacted positively to the announcement. “We look forward to working with Ms. Martin, whose leadership style is known for its openness and responsiveness to employee concerns,” said union spokesperson Emmanuelle Girard.

Veolia Environnement SA employs more than 220,000 people worldwide and provides water, waste, and energy management services in over 50 countries. The company said a formal introduction of Martin to employees and stakeholders will be held at its Paris headquarters next month.
